page: Amazon Web Services m6i.large is a general-purpose virtual server built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, supported by 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. It has 54 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography. This instance does not include local storage or a GPU, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1543.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1804.09. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the lower percentiles, reflecting the constraints of its single physical core. For example, the Geekbench multi-core score is 1806.0, and the uncached memory write bandwidth is 12.92 GB/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m6i.large offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio for entry-level workloads without the overhead of larger instances, though it presents performance tradeoffs for multi-threaded tasks. It is best suited for light general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, single-threaded applications, and small-scale development or testing environments.
